headline: A study finds BF16 and FP16 can produce different greedy LLM outputs
summary: A September 2026 TMLR paper reports that BF16 versus FP16 inference produced different greedy-decoding sequences on 49–100% of prompts across six tested models and three benchmarks. The authors report that recomputing only the language-model output head in FP32 when the top-two logit margin is small improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on an A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 GPUs, with under 4% latency overhead at batch sizes up to 4. They report that the intervention’s benefit disappears at batch size 8 or higher and under end-to-end FP8. These are author-reported results, not an independent reproduction.
